transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. We've got a winter storm coming in and we're looking at operating a remote instruction day tomorrow. I need reports from transportation, IT, nursing, and family engagement before I can sign off on the operating plan. Let's work through each area so we can make sure we've covered instructional delivery, meal access, health support, and family communication. Who'd like to start?

transcript.text: Dr. Lee, I need to flag a critical update for the transportation report. I completed our storm route review this afternoon, and the finding is that no buses can safely travel tomorrow. This means we cannot send meals by regular bus routes as the draft plan currently assumes. Instead, meals can be made available for on-site pickup at North Campus and South Campus from 11:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m. These results have not yet been added to the operations briefing packet, so I wanted to make sure everyone heard this directly before the plan is finalized.

transcript.text: Dr. Lee, I need to flag a critical update for the family engagement report. My family outreach confirmations, completed this week, show that 38 households lack reliable internet access. These households need printed learning packets plus bilingual phone check-ins in Spanish and Somali. The family-access summary is still being compiled and has not yet been added to the draft plan. The draft plan's current assumption that families can use digital materials does not account for these 38 households, and this gap needs to be addressed before the plan is finalized.

transcript.text: Dr. Lee, I need to flag a critical update for the IT report. District learning-management-system authentication will be offline for scheduled maintenance from 8:00 to 11:00 a.m. tomorrow. I confirmed this maintenance window with the vendor today, but the vendor notice has not yet been attached to the remote-day draft plan. This directly conflicts with the draft plan's scheduling of instruction through the LMS beginning at 8:00 a.m. Instead, instructional files must be distributed by email as downloadable PDFs and made available for printing by 7:30 a.m. This change needs to be reflected in the plan before it is finalized.

transcript.text: Thank you all for these critical updates. To summarize what I'm hearing: we have four significant gaps between the draft plan and the on-the-ground reality. From transportation, no buses can safely run, so meal delivery shifts to on-site pickup at North Campus and South Campus, 11 a.m. to 1 p.m. From nursing, we need a staffed nurse hotline from 8 a.m. to noon instead of voicemail. From family engagement, 38 households need printed packets and bilingual phone check-ins. And from IT, LMS authentication is down until 11 a.m., so instruction needs to go out as downloadable PDFs by email by 7:30 a.m. Dr. Lee, all four of these changes need to be incorporated into the operating plan before it's signed. I'd also note that the pickup meal sites and times should be clearly communicated to families alongside the instructional delivery changes, since families will need to know where and when to access meals.
